newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Handelsbanken H1 hints weaker future.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Handelsbanken H1 hints weaker future.

text.p: Swedish bank Handelsbanken posted a strong six-month profit on Tuesday but predicted weaker future earnings as it confirmed sector trends with a disappointing net interest income and lower loan losses.

"Loan losses were lower than expected and net interest income was not as good as we had hoped, which point to the same trends as (rivals) S-E-Banken and Nordbanken," Per Griberg, analyst at Carnegie, told Reuters.

The bank posted a 26 percent rise in operating profit for the first half of the year to 3.78 billion crowns ($471.9 million), beating market expectations of 3.66 billion crowns while S-E-Banken's and Nordbanken's profits came in below expectations.

Loan losses plummeted 75 percent to 234 million crowns, or to 0.1 percent of lending, down from 0.6 percent, outdoing analyst expectations of 428 million crowns and thereby compensating for a lower than expected net interest income.

Net interest income rose 18 percent to 5.39 billion crowns on the back of increased lending volumes following Handelsbanken's acquisition of mortgage lender Stadshypotek for 22.9 billion crowns earlier this year.

"Markedly lower loan losses and a weaker than expected net interest income reflect somewhat weaker earnings, as loan losses will turn up eventually although they could remain low for another couple of years," a Stockholm analyst said.
Analysts did not see much scope for bank shares to rise as all banks indicated weaker future earnings.
"It's debatable whether there is any more potential on share prices, particularly considering that the interest rate trend will be moving upwards," Griberg said.
Handelsbanken shares came off day highs of 254 crowns after the report and were trading 1.5 crowns higher at 249 crowns at 1200 GMT.

Net profits from financial transactions dropped to 233 million crowns from 795 million as a result of lower earnings on interest rate related trading. It rose to 213 million crowns in the second quarter from 20 million in the first quarter.
The fall, also shown by S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, were lower than several analysts had forecast.
"Net of financial transactions were disappointing from all Swedish banks as a strong securities market in the second quarter should have helped them more," a London analyst said.
Net commission income advanced 11 percent to 1.58 billion crowns, mainly helped by increased volumes in fund management and securities trading.
Handelsbanken said margins between lending and deposit interest rates, excluding mortgage lender Stadshypotek, were largely unchanged in the first six months.
"But it is the mortgage margins which have been under pressure and have hurt net interest income," Griberg said.

Costs rose 19 percent to 3.65 billion crowns, of which 13 percentage points derived from the acquisition of Stadshypotek. The rest stemmed from higher systems development costs, setting up new branches in the Nordic region and exchange rate changes.
Swedish branch office operations had unchanged expenses.
The work of integrating Stadshypotek had continued at a fast pace, Handelsbanken said, adding that the extra business with new customers had been much greater than expected.
"During the second quarter the increase in the volume of bank loans has therefore compensated for an anticipated fall in mortgage loans," Handelsbanken said.
"This implies that the group's share of the total Swedish lending market was more or less unchanged during the second quarter at 30.4 percent."
This had a positive impact on net interest income as bank loans have a higher average margin than mortgage loans.

($ = 8.01 Swedish Crowns)
